senses.definition: The portion of a person's name that is generally hereditary or treated as an indicator of a person's family, which may be shared with other members of the family, or otherwise derived from their names in some fashion; distinguished from that person's given name(s).
examples: James is my first name, and Smith is my surname.

quotes.text: In late yeeres Surnames have beene given for Christian names among vs, and no where else in Christendom.
The Norman Conquest...brought with it the novelty of family nomenclature, that is to say, the use of hereditary surnames.
quotes.reference: 1876, E. A. Freeman, The History of the Norman Conquest, V xxv 563:

senses.definition: (obsolete) Synonym of epithet, an additional name, particularly those derived from a birthplace, quality, or achievement.

quotes.reference: 1526, [William Tyndale, transl.], The Newe Testamẽt […] (Tyndale Bible), [Worms, Germany: Peter Schöffer], →OCLC, Acts j:[23]:

quotes.text: My sirname is Peace-Maker, one that is but poorely regarded in England.
quotes.reference: 1590, Richard Harvey, Plaine Percevall the peace-maker of England, Sweetly indeuoring with his blunt persuasions to botch vp a reconciliation between Mar-ton and Mar-tother, B3:

quotes.text:
To his sur-name Coriolanus longs more pride
Then pitty to our Prayers.
quotes.reference: c. 1608–1609 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedy of Coriolanus”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene iii], line 171:

senses.definition: (obsolete) Synonym of nickname, an additional name given to a person, place, or thing, a byname.

quotes.text: I have before declared that Baal was the Sun, and Baal Peor, a sirname, from a particular place of his worship.

senses.definition: (Classical studies) The cognomen of Roman names.

quotes.text: “Lord,” said Sir Launcelot, “I am hight Launcelot, and am surnamed ‘He of the Lake.’”
quotes.reference: 1905, Howard Pyle, “The Story of Launcelot”, in The Story of the Champions of the Round Table, New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, page 66:

quotes.text: The man, surnamed Hsieh (謝), was arrested in the city’s Jhonghe District (中和) on Friday afternoon, after investigators combed through surveillance video footage a day earlier, police said.
